title: Foreign Minister Lin opens Allies Prosperity Trade Office
text:
On November 20, Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung attended the inauguration ceremony of the Allies Prosperity Trade Office (APTO), which took place at Tai-One Space in Hall 1 of the Taipei World Trade Center. APTO is a multifaceted platform tasked with enhancing public-private cooperation on economic and trade exchanges between the ROC (Taiwan) and its diplomatic allies.

The plaque for the new office was jointly unveiled by Minister Lin and representatives of Taiwan’s diplomatic allies, including David Paul, Minister of Finance, Banking and Postal Services of the Marshall Islands; Robert Kennedy Lewis, Ambassador of Saint Lucia; Donya Lynex Francis, Ambassador of Saint Christopher and Nevis; Anjanette Kattil, Ambassador of the Marshall Islands; Lily Tangisia Faavae, Ambassador of Tuvalu; Roudy Stanley Penn, Ambassador of Haiti; Darío Filártiga Ruiz Díaz, Ambassador of Paraguay; Katherine Vanessa Meighan, Ambassador of Belize; Gaafar Sers Jose Uherbelau, Ambassador of Palau; Vulindlela Simphiwe Kunene, Ambassador of Eswatini; and Elroy Wilson, Minister Counsellor at the Embassy of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. The invited ambassadors and Lee Miao-ling, General Manager of Leezen and representative of the Allies Prosperity Trade Company, welcomed the establishment of APTO in their remarks at the event.

Speaking at the opening, Minister Lin said that during his visits to allied nations, he had discovered a wealth of unique, high-quality local products with great market potential. To assist diplomatic allies in introducing these products to the Taiwanese and global markets and to enhance bilateral trade and economic exchanges, Minister Lin said that APTO would serve as a bridge connecting government agencies, businesses, and industry partners and combine the resources of private trading companies to create new opportunities for collaboration.

Minister Lin added that APTO would be a key element of the Diplomatic Allies Prosperity Project and its aim to move beyond traditional assistance and grow partnerships based on mutual benefit. He said that the vision behind the project was for diplomatic relations to yield substantive economic opportunities and shared prosperity, boost economic growth, create jobs, and improve people’s lives.

The Diplomatic Prosperity Project, Minister Lin said, was built on the four key pillars of digital, health, green, and resilience. He stated that by integrating government resources and mobilizing private-sector expertise, the initiative would match Taiwan’s industrial strengths with its allies’ development needs. Minister Lin added that Taiwan was promoting eight flagship initiatives covering semiconductor supply chain resilience, reliable networks and digital governance, sovereign AI, new energy and carbon credit cooperation, smart demonstration parks overseas, smart medicine and health care, smart agriculture, and sustainable tourism. Minister Lin said that these schemes would deepen cooperation and advance mutual prosperity.

APTO will develop two-way markets by participating in international trade shows, bringing high-quality goods from Eswatini and the Pacific to Taiwan, and helping Taiwanese firms enter those markets. Through market research, trade missions, and matchmaking events, APTO will link Taiwanese firms with local partners and build business ties. It will also back public-private partnerships and promote cultural and tourism exchanges.

By matching Taiwan’s industrial strengths with its allies’ development needs, APTO will turn diplomatic ties into opportunities for business and trade cooperation and achieve the vision of shared prosperity. (E)
